result:
**Final search score: 0.5792, against 0.365 for the LRU baseline. I used 10 of the 24 scorer calls.** The answer is in `final.py`.

| | search split (official) | held-out seeds (my local harness) |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline (LRU) | 0.365 | 0.394 |
| First champion (LIRS) | 0.5666 | 0.492 |
| Final pick (ensemble) | **0.5792** | 0.523 |

I had no access to the scorer's held-out split, so the right-hand column uses my own trace generator on seeds I never tuned on. That generator ranked candidates the same way the scorer did each time I checked.

**How it works:** `final.py` runs three policies side by side, each tracking only which keys it would keep: LIRS (handles loops and scans), LRU (handles recency) and W-TinyLFU (handles frequency). Each policy's hits are counted with a decay, so recent hits count most (a window of about 1,000 requests). The real cache follows whichever policy is leading: on a miss it evicts a key the leader has already evicted. It has no hard-coded trace types, so it adapts to whatever the access pattern is doing. Per scorer trace it matches the best single policy on recency (0.847) and shifting loops (0.8275). On loop_and_hot it gives up about 1.5 points to W-TinyLFU alone (0.639 vs 0.6555), because switching between leaders has a cost.

**Approaches tried (local harness score; local LRU was 0.364):**
- ARC: 0.399. W-TinyLFU: 0.334. S3-FIFO: measured only on an earlier version of the harness, where it tied W-TinyLFU. LIRS: 0.478.
- Predicting each key's next access from its past gaps: 0.500 on its own, but it made the ensemble worse because the cache kept switching between leaders.
- Hyperbolic caching: 0.372.
- Frequency-based admission that sometimes skips storing a miss: no gain.
- LIRS that adapts the size of its small queue: 0.508 on its own. In the ensemble it was no better, and on the scorer alone it lost on shifting loops (0.754).
- Tuning the decay and adding a margin before switching leaders: all within ±0.001.

**Candidate log (official calls):**

| Candidate | Score |
|---|---|
| LIRS | 0.5666 |
| W-TinyLFU | 0.5034 |
| ARC | 0.4075 |
| ensemble of LIRS + LRU | 0.5789 |
| ensemble of LIRS + LRU + W-TinyLFU | 0.5792 |
| gap predictor alone | 0.5579 |
| ensemble with gap predictor | 0.5788 |
| adaptive LIRS alone | 0.5649 |
| ensemble with adaptive LIRS | 0.5792 |
| `final.py` | 0.5792 |

I stopped after two rounds that didn't beat the best official score. The remaining headroom is on the hot+scan and mixed traces (about 0.25 hit rate). On my own traces of that kind, the optimal policy (Belady, which sees the future) scores about 0.1 higher.

**Speed:** the official runs finished without hitting the 8-second limit. Locally it takes about 2 µs per request (12 traces of 40k requests in about 0.9 s), but the shared machine made timings noisy.

The working files, harness and every candidate are in `work/`.

Two MCP servers, claude.ai Atlassian Rovo and claude.ai HyperFrames by HeyGen, need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This task didn't need either.
